Abstract: Prefill and decode are complementary in resource usage, but often divergent in parallelism preferences. title: The boundary problem in agentic AI is a platform problem
excerpt:
An autonomous agent will do exactly what its tools let it do, and no more. This sounds like a constraint. In practice it is the whole risk, because the set of things an agent’s tools let it do is almost never the set anyone deliberately chose. It is the set that accumulated. A tool added for one workflow stays available for every workflow. A credential scoped for a demo survives into production. A delegation added to unblock a Friday deploy becomes a permanent edge in the graph. Nobody decides to give the agent that reach. There was never a moment where reach was decided at all.
This is the pattern worth naming. It is not a bug in any particular agent framework and it will not be fixed by a better prompt. Across enough deployments the same shape recurs: authority is granted incrementally, locally, and invisibly, and the system’s actual power drifts steadily away from anyone’s model of what it should be able to do. The agents behave. The boundaries erode anyway. By the time someone asks “wait, can it do that?”, the honest answer is usually “it could for weeks, and we only noticed now.”

title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
excerpt:
A video player seeking to the middle of a movie asks for a few megabytes. Under our old range caching, that one request could make Cloudflare pull 128 MiB from the origin and move it between data centers, sometimes after the viewer had already left. Range requests are how large files get delivered, and caching them naively easily leads to wasted network bandwidth and wasted disk operations when running a CDN at scale.
So we rebuilt how our cache handles them. For R2, Cloudflare's object storage, p99 time to first byte dropped by about half, and a follow-up improvement cut tiered cache  traffic for R2 and similar workloads by about 6%.
Today, we're making that new implementation available as Origin Range Requests , a self-service feature on all plans. There's no range size to tune and no need to contact support. Turn it on with a Cache Rule , and Cloudflare handles the rest.
